 Padikkal's fifty rescues India A on Day 2 after Rahul, Jaiswal fail again!
 By REDIFF CRICKET 
 Updated: October 25, 2026 11:31 IST 
 3 Minutes Read 
 Summarize this -->
 Listen to this article 
 Watch on Rediff TV 
 Share this Article 
 x 
 Devdutt Padikkal's resilient half-century provided a much-needed boost for India A, helping them recover from an early collapse against New Zealand A on Day 2 of the unofficial Test. 
 IMAGE: Devdutt Padikkal scored a half-century to rescue India A in their second innings on Day 2 of the 1st unofficial Test against New Zealand on Sunday. Photograph: ANI Photo 
 Key Points
 India A finished Day 2 at 98/2 in their second innings, trailing New Zealand A by 106 runs.
 Devdutt Padikkal scored a crucial half-century (50 off 65 balls) and shared an 88-run stand with Sai Sudharsan (35*).
 India A's openers, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rahul, were dismissed cheaply for the second time in the match.
 New Zealand A posted a strong total of 317 in their first innings, securing a 204-run lead.
 Anshul Kamboj and Auqib Nabi were the pick of the bowlers for India A, taking three wickets each.
 Devdutt Padikkal stroked an unbeaten half-century to rescue India A on Day 2 of the first unofficial Test against New Zealand A at Bert Sutcliffe Oval, Lincoln, on Sunday.
 Padikkal, who was dropped on 19 in the slips, made most to be unbeaten on 56 at stumps on the second day.
 India A, who lost their openers early, recovered to 106/2 at second on the second day. They still trail New Zealand A by 98 runs.
 Padikkal put on a vital stand of 88 runs for the third wicket with Sai Sudharsan, who made a patient 39 not out, as the two left-handers scripted India's brilliant fightback on the second day.
 New Zealand piled on the runs on the second day as they posted a huge 317 in their first innings to take a huge 204-run first innings lead.
 India A's Top-Order Collapse
 India A got off to a horror start in their second innings, as they lost their openers failed for the second time in the match.
 Yashasvi Jaiswal was caught behind for five off his gloves after he failed to evade the incoming short ball from fast bowler Simon Keene.
 In the very next over, Rahul was dismissed hit wicket off Fraser Sheat for five to leave India reeling on 10/2 in the fifth over.
 Lower Order Resistance for New Zealand A
 Earlier, New Zealand A's lower order frustrated the Indians. Dean Foxcroft stroked 51, while Mitchell Hay (24) and Kristian Clarke smashed 42 with the last four wickets adding 112 runs for the hosts.
 For India, pacers Anshul Kamboj (3/52) and Auqib Nabi (3/69) picked up three wickets each, while Akash Deep claimed 2/57 and Mukesh Choudhary and Washington Sundar got one wicket each.
